commit.message: Turn a finding green when the fix is confirmed (0.6.0)

findings.title: Carried and fresh findings collide on id
findings.description: `numberFindings` (engine/src/review.ts:354) re-issues ids as `f1..fN` for every review, so `previous` and `fresh` both start at `f1`. Merging them here produces duplicate ids whenever anything carries forward. Downstream everything keys on id alone: `restoreFixed(done, resolvedIds)` will render a brand-new `f1` as "fixed · confirmed" because a carried `f1` was confirmed, `diagnostics.remove(id)` drops both squiggles, and `markFixed` ticks both rows. That is precisely the false-green this module's own docblock says is worse than leaving a finding open. The new qa test avoids it by giving fresh findings `n1..n3`.
findings.suggestion: Consider making ids unique across the merge — e.g. re-key carried findings to a namespaced id (`prev:f1`, or a content hash of file+title) before returning, and map `resolvedIds` through the same rewrite so the ids the panel receives still refer to the carried copies.

findings.title: No deterministic test for the verify response handling
findings.description: The only coverage for this path is `extension/test/demo-green.js`, which needs a real repository and a live Claude call. The branches that matter most are cheap to test in isolation and currently untested: the string-vs-object `envelope.result` unwrap, the `known.has(id)` filter that stops the model naming an id it was never given, and the catch-all returning `[]`. A regression in the unwrap would silently return no confirmations, which looks identical to "nothing was fixed".
findings.suggestion: Consider adding unit tests around the parsing/filtering half — either by extracting it into an exported pure function taking `stdout` and the prior list, or by pointing `claudePath` at a small script that echoes canned envelopes.

findings.title: Findings stay off screen until the verify call returns
findings.description: `verifyFixes` is awaited before `display`, so the fresh findings — already computed — are withheld for the duration of a second Claude invocation. It inherits the full review timeout (`cfg.timeoutMs ?? 600_000`), so a hung verify can leave the panel empty for ten minutes after a review that has already finished, with the status bar still reading "Reviewing".
findings.suggestion: Consider displaying `result.findings` immediately, then re-displaying with the reconciled list once verification returns; and giving verification its own, much shorter budget than the review timeout since it only re-reads a diff.

findings.title: Overlap denominator lets a short title swallow an unrelated finding
findings.description: `overlap` divides by `Math.min(a.size, b.size)`, so a two-word signature reaches 1.0 against any longer title sharing those two words in the same file. When `sameProblem` matches wrongly, the old finding is `continue`d at line 71 — it vanishes from the list entirely without ever being marked fixed, which is the silent-disappearance case this file is written to avoid. A short title like "Unbounded loop" would match "Loop bound is unbounded in the writer".
findings.suggestion: Consider a Jaccard ratio (shared / union size) instead, or requiring a minimum signature size before a match is allowed, so two-word titles cannot reach the 0.6 threshold on partial evidence.

findings.title: `verified` survives a new review while `fixed` is cleared
findings.description: `setFindings` clears `this.fixed` but not `this.verified`, and `display` only calls `restoreFixed` when `done.length` is non-zero (extension.ts:132). After a review with nothing resolved, `verified` still holds the previous review's ids. Since ids restart at `f1` each review, a developer who then hand-ticks `f1` sees "fixed · confirmed" and a tooltip saying the reviewer re-read the file — a claim nothing supports, and exactly the distinction the new docblock says matters.
findings.suggestion: Consider clearing `this.verified` in `setFindings` alongside `this.fixed`, so the confirmed set can never outlive the findings it described.

findings.title: Reviewer-confirmed greens are not persisted
findings.description: `onProgress` only fires from the `onFixedChanged` handler, i.e. on a developer toggle. Ids that went green because the reviewer confirmed them are never written to `PROGRESS_KEY`, so after a window reload `restoreProgress(sha)` returns without them and those rows come back open.
findings.suggestion: Consider calling `this.onProgress?.(sha, done)` here when `resolvedIds.length` is non-zero, so a confirmed fix survives a reload the same way a hand-ticked one does.

findings.title: Status bar and log count only the fresh findings
findings.description: The panel now shows `onScreen` (fresh plus carried), but `status.reviewed` and the log line still report `result.findings.length`. With anything carried forward, the status bar says one number while the tree badge and title say another.
findings.suggestion: Consider reporting the outstanding count from the reconciled list — e.g. `onScreen.length - resolvedIds.length` — so the two surfaces agree on what is left to address.
